access.title: Access for Grok Bot
access.description:
Grok Bot answers and acts in Home Assistant through an MCP connector you add in the Grok Bot app. Detected: **{mcp_status}**.

**Recommended: HA-MCP.** Copy the remote URL from HA-MCP → Configure and add it as a Home Assistant connector in the Grok Bot app.
**Fallback: core MCP Server.** Connector URL `{connector_url}` with OAuth or a long-lived access token. The LLM API you pick there (Assist = only exposed entities) decides what Grok Bot can touch.

The URL must be reachable from the internet (Nabu Casa or your external URL). The access webhook is an Advanced alternative; its level only applies to that webhook (current URL: {access_url}).

data_description.access_method: HA-MCP (or core MCP Server) is the default: Grok Bot uses your MCP connector and calls grok_bot.reply. The access webhook is for instances without an MCP connector.
data_description.access_level: Only used by the access webhook. Restarts, Supervisor/host actions and deleting integrations are always blocked.

install_mcp.title: Install HA-MCP first
install_mcp.description:
**Install HA-MCP first.** Without an MCP connector Grok Bot can receive your messages but can't answer or fix anything in Home Assistant.

1. [Install HA-MCP]({ha_mcp_install_url}) via HACS / the Marketplace and restart Home Assistant.
2. [Add the HA-MCP integration]({ha_mcp_setup_url}) and create its server entry.
3. Open Grok Bot's options → Access again: it detects HA-MCP and shows a ready-to-paste prompt to connect it in the Grok Bot app.

Prefer the built-in option? [Set up core MCP Server]({mcp_setup_url}) instead. You can continue now: Grok Bot stays reply-only until a connector is set up.

data_description.access_method: HA-MCP (or core MCP Server) is the default: Grok Bot uses your MCP connector and calls grok_bot.reply. The access webhook is for instances without an MCP connector.
data_description.access_level: Only used by the access webhook. Restarts, Supervisor/host actions and deleting integrations are always blocked.

connect.title: Connect it in Grok Bot
connect.description:
HA-MCP is installed. **Before you use Grok Bot, connect this Home Assistant ("{name}") in the Grok Bot app.**

Copy the prompt below and send it to your Grok Bot. It connects this HA through HA-MCP (`{mcp_url}`), sets up the webhook routine with safe rules and replies "Connected". Until then a "Grok Bot not connected yet" repair stays open. You can show this prompt again with the "Show Grok Bot setup prompt" button.

```
{prompt}
```

access.description:

data.access_require_pending: Only while a request is open

data_description.access_method: HA-MCP (or core MCP Server) is the default: Grok Bot uses your MCP connector and calls grok_bot.reply. The access webhook is for instances without an MCP connector.
data_description.access_level: Only used by the access webhook. Restarts, Supervisor/host actions and deleting integrations are always blocked.
data_description.reply_timeout: After this many minutes an awaiting request counts as answered in the Grok Bot app (0 = never).
data_description.trusted: 🚩 RISKY. Off by default. Lets Grok Bot edit configuration.yaml, automations.yaml, scripts.yaml, scenes.yaml and files under packages/ (never secrets.yaml, .storage or custom_components) and restart Home Assistant, only for fix requests and only while the Trusted access switch is on. A wrong edit can stop Home Assistant from starting. A backup is made before every edit (/config/.grok_bot_backups) and restarts only happen after a successful config check.
data_description.trusted_confirm: Required to turn on Trusted access.
data_description.trusted_duration: How long the Trusted access switch stays on before it turns itself off (default 30 minutes). 🚩🚩 Always on: Grok Bot may edit configuration files and restart Home Assistant for every fix request, at any time, until you switch it off yourself. Only choose this on a system you can restore.

mcp_server_missing.title: Install HA-MCP so Grok Bot can answer
mcp_server_missing.description: No MCP server was found, so Grok Bot can't answer or act in Home Assistant. [Install HA-MCP]({ha_mcp_install_url}) (recommended) and [add it]({ha_mcp_setup_url}), or [set up core MCP Server]({mcp_setup_url}) (connector path `{mcp_path}`). Then open the Grok Bot options → Access.

not_connected.title: Grok Bot not connected yet
not_connected.description: HA-MCP is installed, but "{name}" has not received a reply from Grok Bot yet. Press the "Show Grok Bot setup prompt" button (or open the options → Connect it in Grok Bot), send the prompt to your Grok Bot and wait for "Connected". This repair clears itself on the first grok_bot.reply.

trusted_always_on.title: Grok Bot Trusted access is always on
trusted_always_on.description: Trusted access for "{name}" is set to Always on: Grok Bot may edit configuration files and restart Home Assistant for every fix request. Switch off Trusted access or pick a time window in Configure → Access when you no longer need it.
